newsitem.title: USA: U.S. F-16 fired missile at Iraqi air defense.
newsitem.headline: U.S. F-16 fired missile at Iraqi air defense.

text.p: A U.S. Air Force F-16 jet enforcing a no-fly zone in southern Iraq was targeted by Iraqi radar and fired on the Iraqi installation in response, the White House confirmed late on Saturday.

The plane returned to base without incident. President Bill Clinton was informed of the incident, which took place about 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT), early on Saturday, White House spokesman Barry Toiv said.

The spokesman said the pilot of the F-16 believed he had been illuminated by the missile-tracking radar of the mobile surface-to-air missile battery, a hostile act that allows U.S. pilots to fire missiles in retaliation.
The F-16 pilot fired a single High-speed Anti-Radiation Missile (HARM) at what he believed was a mobile surface-to-air missile battery.

The Washington Times, which reported the incident, said there was apparently some question about whether the pilot was actually illuminated by the Iraqi air-defence battery, and the U.S. Central Command was investigating the incident.
The no-fly zone was extended from the 32nd parallel to the 33rd parallel early last month after an Iraqi military drive into Kurdish-held northern Iraq, in support of pro-Iraqi Kurdish separatists.
